recommendation: Design guidance, not a WCAG minimum: 16 px / 1rem is a common starting body size. 1.4.4 sets no minimum size; it requires text to resize up to 200% without assistive technology and without loss of content or functionality (exceptions: captions and images of text)
rationale: Context-dependent. Smaller text is not a 1.4.4 failure by itself and rem does not guarantee accessibility; test resizing instead

recommendation: Design guidance: about 1.5 is a common starting line height. 1.4.12 requires no loss of content or functionality when the user sets line height to at least 1.5x font size together with the other three spacing values
rationale: Tests tolerance to user overrides; the initial authored value is not the requirement

recommendation: Design guidance: clear paragraph spacing helps grouping. 1.4.12 requires no loss of content or functionality when the user sets spacing after paragraphs to at least 2x font size together with the other three spacing values
rationale: Tests tolerance to user overrides; content need not start with this value

recommendation: Tolerate user-set letter spacing of at least 0.12x font size without loss of content or functionality (applied together with line, paragraph and word spacing)
rationale: User override tolerance; the page need not offer its own control. Languages and scripts without a property may conform using only the properties they use

recommendation: Tolerate user-set word spacing of at least 0.16x font size without loss of content or functionality (applied together with line, paragraph and letter spacing)
rationale: User override tolerance; the page need not offer its own control. Languages and scripts without a property may conform using only the properties they use

recommendation: Design guidance: 45-75 characters per line is a common readability target, not a WCAG requirement. AAA 1.4.8 requires a mechanism (page or user agent) for width of no more than 80 characters (40 for CJK)
rationale: Not an AA requirement; 1.4.8 also covers colors, justification, spacing and 200% resize without horizontal scrolling

recommendation: Design guidance: avoid fully justified blocks and align to the start edge of the writing direction (left in LTR, right in RTL). AAA 1.4.8 requires a mechanism so text is not justified; it does not dictate the default appearance
rationale: Justification can create uneven word gaps; AA does not prohibit justified text

recommendation: Readable at 320 CSS px wide without horizontal scroll
rationale: Zoom and mobile usability

recommendation: Text can be resized up to 200% without assistive technology and without loss of content or functionality (exceptions: captions and images of text)
rationale: Browser zoom or text-only resizing can satisfy it; do not block user agent scaling. Check intermediate steps and each responsive layout

recommendation: 4.5:1 against background
rationale: AA minimum

recommendation: 3:1 against background (18pt or 14pt bold)
rationale: AA large text minimum

recommendation: Do not convey info by color alone (e.g., error = red)
rationale: Color blind users cannot perceive

recommendation: Use font-display swap; fallback readable
rationale: Avoids invisible text while loading

recommendation: Do not set uppercase for long blocks
rationale: Screen readers may spell letters; slower reading

recommendation: Design guidance: prefer regular or heavier weights for body text; very thin strokes can look weaker than their measured contrast
rationale: 1.4.3 sets no minimum weight. Size and bold together classify large text (at least 18 pt or 14 pt bold) so AA needs 4.5:1 normal and 3:1 large text with its exceptions. Very thin strokes may benefit from heavier strokes or more contrast: a legibility recommendation not a mandatory weight

recommendation: Reserve for emphasis; avoid blocks of italic
rationale: Reduced legibility especially in dyslexia

recommendation: Design guidance: choose a face with clearly distinguishable letterforms and test with your audience. No WCAG criterion requires a specific face
rationale: Benefits of any one typeface are not guaranteed for every reader; do not treat a font as a compliance measure

recommendation: Use decorative faces only for display headlines
rationale: Low legibility in long copy

recommendation: Use real text not images of text except logos
rationale: Zoom and AT cannot handle image text

recommendation: Underline links in body copy; contrast 3:1 vs text and 4.5:1 vs background
rationale: Color alone insufficient for color blind
